items.headline: FBI warns ARTEX AI hacking tool is powering global cyberattacks
items.summary: The FBI is warning that hackers are using an AI-powered penetration testing framework called ARTEX to automate cyberattacks against organizations worldwide, including a recent ConnectWise supply-chain breach that compromised Microsoft 365 customer environments. [...]
lines: Reported by BleepingComputer: The FBI is warning that hackers are using an AI-powered penetration testing framework called ARTEX to automate cyberattacks against organizations worldwide.
The warning cites a recent ConnectWise supply-chain breach that compromised Microsoft 365 customer environments.
For IT teams, the report links automated attack tooling to a supply-chain breach that affected Microsoft 365 customer environments.

lines: Reported by The Hacker News: Amazon's threat intelligence team uncovered an AI agent campaign that targets internet-exposed AI apps such as LiteLLM, One API, and Dify to steal stored AI provider keys.
The attackers' AI agents' own records, captured by Amazon using decoy servers, describe stolen keys being used to run the AI models that powered the search for more keys.
For IT teams, AI apps exposed to the internet and the API keys stored inside them are a target for automated attacks.

items.headline: BO Team Exploits Log4Shell in VMware vCenter, Compromises Russian Firm's Code-Signing Server

lines: Reported by The Hacker News: Kaspersky's ICS CERT team documented a months-long compromise of a Russian software developer's development infrastructure and a code-signing server.
The developer contacted Kaspersky in June 2025, and the activity has been attributed to a threat actor named BO Team, also known as Black Owl and Hoody Hyena.
For IT teams, the compromise of a code-signing server is a risk because attackers who control signing infrastructure can sign malicious software that appears legitimate.

lines: Indian engineers at Samsung Research Institute–Noida (SRI-N) worked on auto cycle detection for the Galaxy Watch during its development.

lines: Reported by The Hacker News: Six unpatched flaws in Danfoss AK-SM800A refrigeration controllers could let a remote attacker take over a controller without logging in, according to Dutch security consultancy Midnight Blue.
No patch is available, and the researchers say the newest firmware, version 5.4.0, does not fix the flaws.
Cybersecurity agencies in Belgium, Ireland and Germany told operators this week, according to the report.
Operators of these controllers face exposure with no available patch, which matters for facilities and IT teams that manage them.

items.headline: New NoisyTCP vulnerability lets attackers crash Linux servers
items.summary: An 11-year-old Linux kernel vulnerability, dubbed NoisyTCP, affects almost all Linux distributions and lets attackers crash systems running Nginx, Apache, and SSH servers with default configurations. [...]
lines: Reported by BleepingComputer: A new vulnerability named NoisyTCP, an 11-year-old Linux kernel flaw, affects almost all Linux distributions.
It lets attackers crash systems running Nginx, Apache, and SSH servers with default configurations.
IT teams running Linux servers with these services in default configurations may want to review their exposure.

lines: Reported by The Hacker News: A Linux-focused cryptomining operation tracked as REF3364 uses a modified NVIDIA library to hide GPU activity.
Its central toolkit, SANSAR, is a Rust-based orchestrator that receives commands over the TOR anonymity network to manage CPU and GPU miners.
